## Task statement

**Invariant.** 0 known vulns ≥ high in runtime deps; actions SHA-pinned; cooldown set

**Oracle.** `pip-audit`/`npm audit`; YAML checks

**Violation cases seeded.** known-vulnerable pin; mutable action tag

Source: `EVALS-PLAN.md` Layer 0.

## Construction

Every task is a directory `evals/cases/P7/<case>/` holding a `case.yaml` (the task record: `id`, `property`, `origin`, `grader`, `expect`, `description`, `canary`), a `vuln/` tree with exactly one planted violation, and a `clean/` twin — the same code with the violation fixed through the toolkit primitive. The grader scores both: the violation must be detected in `vuln/` (recall) and not in `clean/` (precision), so the clean twin is the baseline scored alongside every task.

Origins, in the priority order of EVALS-PLAN.md Layer 2:

- **historical-miss** (3): a real miss from this program, encoded permanently.
- **derived** (2): a violation case from the Layer 0 row, in a code shape the historical cases do not already cover.

| task | origin | grader | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `P7-dependabot-no-cooldown-01` | historical-miss | `supply` | Dependabot switched on with the two-line default: no cooldown, so every fresh release (the ones most often yanked) was proposed the morning it shipped, ~37 PRs in the first week. clean is the toolkit template: each ecosystem waits 7 days after a release and groups minor/patch bumps. |
| `P7-known-vuln-pin-01` | historical-miss | `supply` | smart-dispatch requirements before PR #29: Flask 2.3.3, Flask-CORS 4.0.0 and scikit-learn 1.3.0, all below the versions the audit demanded. clean carries the bumped pins. Note the scikit-learn choice: "latest" (1.9) is CVE-clean but cannot load the served joblib artefact trained under 1.6.1, so the fix is the audited version that matches the artefact, with the reason written next to the pin. |
| `P7-known-vuln-range-02` | derived | `supply` | The same packages as lower-bounded ranges in a minimal requirements file: a floor below the audited version admits the vulnerable release. clean raises the floor and bounds the upper side to the tested minor. |
| `P7-mutable-action-tag-01` | historical-miss | `supply` | Every project's workflow before the SHA-pinning round: actions referenced by a moving tag (@v4), which the action's owner, or whoever holds their token, can repoint. clean pins each action to a full commit SHA with the version in a trailing comment so Dependabot keeps bumping it. |
| `P7-mutable-reusable-workflow-02` | derived | `supply` | The other `uses:` shape: a job that calls the toolkit's reusable workflow by branch (@main), so every push to the toolkit changes what runs in this repo's CI. clean pins the call to a commit SHA with the release in the comment; the steps that stay local (./.github/...) are exempt. |

## Metrics and current numbers

- **recall** = tasks whose `vuln/` the grader detected ÷ tasks, Wilson 95% CI.
- **precision** = tasks whose `clean/` the grader did not flag ÷ tasks, Wilson 95% CI.
- with `--trials K > 1`: **pass@k** (any of k) and **pass^k** (all of k) over tasks.

## Known limitations

From the grader docstrings (what each oracle can and cannot decide):

### `supply`

> P7 supply-chain grader (plugin): offline checks of the files that decide
> what gets installed and run.
>
>     supply  expect: {kind: audit | actions | dependabot}
>
>     audit       every `requirements*.txt` under the variant dir is read; each
>                 pinned (`==`) or lower-bounded (`>=`, `~=`) version is compared
>                 with `evals/fixtures/supply/known_vuln_pins.json`, built from
>                 the pins this program actually had to bump. Detected = a
>                 requirement whose minimum installable version is below the
>                 fixture's `min_ok`. Bare names are recorded as `unpinned`, not
>                 detected (that is a reproducibility problem, not a known vuln).
>     actions     every `*.yml`/`*.yaml` under the variant dir; each `uses:` that
>                 is not local (`./`) or `docker://` must be pinned to a 40-hex
>                 commit SHA. Detected = a mutable ref (tag, branch, or none).
>                 SHAs without a trailing `# vX.Y.Z` comment are recorded (Dependabot
>                 needs the comment to keep bumping) but not detected.
>     dependabot  `dependabot.yml` under the variant dir; every `updates[]` entry
>                 must set `cooldown.default-days` >= 1. Detected = one that does
>                 not (the config that opened ~37 PRs in a week).

## Contamination policy

- **Canary.** Every `case.yaml`, every registry entry and `tasks.jsonl` carry the string in `evals/registry/CANARY.txt` (BIG-bench convention): a model that can reproduce it has seen this corpus in training, and its scores on it do not measure the property.
- **Split.** This eval is `split: build`. Build-split cases are used to tune rules and defenses. The held-out split (`evals/heldout/`, EVALS-PLAN.md Phase 4) is sealed: written after the defenses, never used for tuning, and scored only in reports.
- **No model in the loop.** Every grader is deterministic code; no LLM judges a result, so there is nothing to contaminate on the grading side.
